Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He was also King of _____ from 781
Louis the Pious.fact: He was also King of Aquitaine from 781. During his reign in Aquitaine, Louis was charged with the defence of the empire's southwestern frontier.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: During his reign in _____, Louis was charged with the defence of the empire's southwestern frontier
Louis the Pious.fact: He was also King of Aquitaine from 781. During his reign in Aquitaine, Louis was charged with the defence of the empire's southwestern frontier.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: As the only surviving son of _____ and Hildegard, he became the sole ruler of the Franks after his father's death in 814
Louis the Pious.fact: Louis the Pious (Latin: Hludowicus Pius; French: Louis le Pieux; German: Ludwig der Fromme; 778 – 20 June 840), also called the Fair and the Debonaire, was King of the Franks and co-emperor with his father, Charlemagne, from 813. As the only surviving son of Charlemagne and Hildegard, he became the sole ruler of the Franks after his father's death in 814.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He held this position until his death in 840, save for _____ 833 to March 834 when Louis was deposed
Louis the Pious.fact: He held this position until his death in 840, save for November 833 to March 834 when Louis was deposed.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He conquered _____ from the Emirate of Córdoba in 801 and asserted Frankish authority over Pamplona and the Basques south of the Pyrenees in 812
Louis the Pious.fact: He conquered Barcelona from the Emirate of Córdoba in 801 and asserted Frankish authority over Pamplona and the Basques south of the Pyrenees in 812.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: As emperor, he included his adult sons, _____, Pepin and Louis, in the government and sought to establish a suitable division of the realm among them
Louis the Pious.fact: As emperor, he included his adult sons, Lothair, Pepin and Louis, in the government and sought to establish a suitable division of the realm among them.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: In the 830s his empire was torn by civil war between his sons that was only exacerbated by Louis's attempts to include his son _____ by his second wife in the succession plans
Louis the Pious.fact: In the 830s his empire was torn by civil war between his sons that was only exacerbated by Louis's attempts to include his son Charles by his second wife in the succession plans.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He was the third son of _____ by his wife Hildegard
Louis the Pious.fact: He was the third son of Charlemagne by his wife Hildegard.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He had a twin brother named _____, who died young
Louis the Pious.fact: He had a twin brother named Lothair, who died young. Louis and Lothair were given names from the old Merovingian dynasty, possibly to suggest a connection.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Louis and _____ were given names from the old Merovingian dynasty, possibly to suggest a connection
Louis the Pious.fact: He had a twin brother named Lothair, who died young. Louis and Lothair were given names from the old Merovingian dynasty, possibly to suggest a connection.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Louis was crowned King of _____ as a three-year-old child in 781
Louis the Pious.fact: Louis was crowned King of Aquitaine as a three-year-old child in 781. In the following year he was sent to Aquitaine accompanied by regents and a court.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: In the following year he was sent to _____ accompanied by regents and a court
Louis the Pious.fact: Louis was crowned King of Aquitaine as a three-year-old child in 781. In the following year he was sent to Aquitaine accompanied by regents and a court.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Charlemagne constituted this sub-kingdom in order to secure the border of his realm after the destructive war against the _____ and Basques under Waifar (capitulated c
Louis the Pious.fact: Charlemagne constituted this sub-kingdom in order to secure the border of his realm after the destructive war against the Aquitanians and Basques under Waifar (capitulated c.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: 768) and later _____ II, which culminated in the disastrous Battle of Roncesvalles (778)
Louis the Pious.fact: 768) and later Hunald II, which culminated in the disastrous Battle of Roncesvalles (778).

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: However, wary of the customs his son may have been assimilating into in _____, Charlemagne, who had remarried to Fastrada after the death of Hildegard, sent for Louis in 785
Louis the Pious.fact: However, wary of the customs his son may have been assimilating into in Aquitaine, Charlemagne, who had remarried to Fastrada after the death of Hildegard, sent for Louis in 785.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: In 794, _____ gave four former Gallo-Roman villas to Louis, in the thought that he would take in each in turn as winter residence: Doué, Ebreuil, Angeac and the Chasseneuil
Louis the Pious.fact: Charlemagne wanted Louis to grow up in the area where he was to reign. However, wary of the customs his son may have been assimilating into in Aquitaine, Charlemagne, who had remarried to Fastrada after the death of Hildegard, sent for Louis in 785.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Louis reigned over the _____
Louis the Pious.fact: Louis reigned over the Spanish March.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: In 797, _____, the largest city of the Marca, fell to the Franks when Zeid, its governor, rebelled against Córdoba and, failing, handed it to them
Louis the Pious.fact: In 797, Barcelona, the largest city of the Marca, fell to the Franks when Zeid, its governor, rebelled against Córdoba and, failing, handed it to them.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: However, the princes were not given independence from central authority as _____ wished to implant in them the concepts of empire and unity by sending them on remote military expeditions
Louis the Pious.fact: However, the princes were not given independence from central authority as Charlemagne wished to implant in them the concepts of empire and unity by sending them on remote military expeditions. Louis was one of Charlemagne's three legitimate sons to survive infancy.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Louis was one of _____'s three legitimate sons to survive infancy
Louis the Pious.fact: However, the princes were not given independence from central authority as Charlemagne wished to implant in them the concepts of empire and unity by sending them on remote military expeditions. Louis was one of Charlemagne's three legitimate sons to survive infancy.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Louis joined his brother _____ at the Mezzogiorno campaign in Italy against the Duke Grimoald of Benevento at least once
Louis the Pious.fact: Louis joined his brother Pippin at the Mezzogiorno campaign in Italy against the Duke Grimoald of Benevento at least once.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: His twin brother, _____, died during infancy
Louis the Pious.fact: His twin brother, Lothair, died during infancy.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: According to the _____ custom of partible inheritance, Louis had expected to share his inheritance with his brothers, Charles the Younger, King of Neustria, and Pepin, King of Italy
Louis the Pious.fact: According to the Frankish custom of partible inheritance, Louis had expected to share his inheritance with his brothers, Charles the Younger, King of Neustria, and Pepin, King of Italy. In the Divisio Regnorum of 806, Charlemagne had slated Charles the Younger as his successor as ruler of the Frankish heartland of Neustria and Austrasia, while giving Pepin the Iron Crown of Lombardy, which Charlemagne possessed by conquest.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: However, _____'s other legitimate sons died—Pepin in 810 and Charles in 811—and Louis was crowned co-emperor with an already ailing Charlemagne in Aachen on 11 September 813
Louis the Pious.fact: In the Divisio Regnorum of 806, Charlemagne had slated Charles the Younger as his successor as ruler of the Frankish heartland of Neustria and Austrasia, while giving Pepin the Iron Crown of Lombardy, which Charlemagne possessed by conquest. However, Charlemagne's other legitimate sons died—Pepin in 810 and Charles in 811—and Louis was crowned co-emperor with an already ailing Charlemagne in Aachen on 11 September 813.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He rushed to _____ and crowned himself emperor to shouts of Vivat Imperator Ludovicus by the attending nobles
Louis the Pious.fact: However, Charlemagne's other legitimate sons died—Pepin in 810 and Charles in 811—and Louis was crowned co-emperor with an already ailing Charlemagne in Aachen on 11 September 813. He rushed to Aachen and crowned himself emperor to shouts of Vivat Imperator Ludovicus by the attending nobles.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Upon arriving at the imperial court in _____ in an atmosphere of suspicion and anxiety on both sides, Louis's first act was to purge the palace of what he considered undesirable
Louis the Pious.fact: However, Charlemagne's other legitimate sons died—Pepin in 810 and Charles in 811—and Louis was crowned co-emperor with an already ailing Charlemagne in Aachen on 11 September 813. He rushed to Aachen and crowned himself emperor to shouts of Vivat Imperator Ludovicus by the attending nobles.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He destroyed the old _____ pagan tokens and texts which had been collected by Charlemagne
Louis the Pious.fact: He destroyed the old Germanic pagan tokens and texts which had been collected by Charlemagne.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He made _____, margrave of Septimania, and Ebbo, Archbishop of Reims his chief counsellors
Louis the Pious.fact: He made Bernard, margrave of Septimania, and Ebbo, Archbishop of Reims his chief counsellors.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He retained some of his father's ministers, such as _____, abbot of St
Louis the Pious.fact: He retained some of his father's ministers, such as Elisachar, abbot of St. Later he replaced Elisachar with Hildwin, abbot of many monasteries.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Later he replaced _____ with Hildwin, abbot of many monasteries
Louis the Pious.fact: He retained some of his father's ministers, such as Elisachar, abbot of St. Later he replaced Elisachar with Hildwin, abbot of many monasteries.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Maximin near Trier, and _____, Archbishop of Cologne
Louis the Pious.fact: Maximin near Trier, and Hildebold, Archbishop of Cologne.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: One of _____'s primary reforms was to ensure that all religious houses in Louis's realm adhered to the Rule of Saint Benedict, named for its creator, Benedict of Nursia
Louis the Pious.fact: He also employed Benedict of Aniane (the Second Benedict), a Septimanian Visigoth, whom he made abbot of the newly set up Inden Monastery at Aix-la-Chapelle and charged him with the reform of the Frankish church. One of Benedict's primary reforms was to ensure that all religious houses in Louis's realm adhered to the Rule of Saint Benedict, named for its creator, Benedict of Nursia.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: From the start of his reign, his coinage imitated his father _____'s portrait, which gave it an image of imperial authority and prestige
Louis the Pious.fact: From the start of his reign, his coinage imitated his father Charlemagne's portrait, which gave it an image of imperial authority and prestige.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: In 816, _____ IV, who had succeeded Leo III, visited Reims and again crowned Louis on Sunday 5 October
Louis the Pious.fact: In 816, Pope Stephen IV, who had succeeded Leo III, visited Reims and again crowned Louis on Sunday 5 October.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: The term _____ is a modern (19th-century) creation
Louis the Pious.fact: Three months later among the approval of his Aachen court and the clergy he issued an imperial decree of eighteen chapters, the Ordinatio Imperii, that laid out plans for an orderly dynastic succession. The term Ordinatio Imperii is a modern (19th-century) creation.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He proceeded to divide the empire among his three sons: _____ was proclaimed and crowned co-emperor in Aachen by his father
Louis the Pious.fact: In 815, Louis had already given his two eldest sons a share in the government, when he had sent his elder sons Lothair and Pepin to govern Bavaria and Aquitaine, respectively, though without the royal titles. He proceeded to divide the empire among his three sons: Lothair was proclaimed and crowned co-emperor in Aachen by his father.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He was promised the succession to most of the _____ dominions (excluding the exceptions below), and would be the overlord of his brothers and cousin
Louis the Pious.fact: He was promised the succession to most of the Frankish dominions (excluding the exceptions below), and would be the overlord of his brothers and cousin.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Pepin was proclaimed King of _____, his territory including Gascony, the march around Toulouse, and the counties of Carcassonne, Autun, Avallon and Nevers
Louis the Pious.fact: In 815, Louis had already given his two eldest sons a share in the government, when he had sent his elder sons Lothair and Pepin to govern Bavaria and Aquitaine, respectively, though without the royal titles. Pepin was proclaimed King of Aquitaine, his territory including Gascony, the march around Toulouse, and the counties of Carcassonne, Autun, Avallon and Nevers.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Louis, the youngest son, was proclaimed King of _____ and the neighbouring marches
Louis the Pious.fact: Louis, the youngest son, was proclaimed King of Bavaria and the neighbouring marches.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: If he died childless, _____ would inherit his kingdom
Louis the Pious.fact: If he died childless, Lothair would inherit his kingdom. In the event of Lothair dying without sons, one of Louis the Pious's younger sons would be chosen to replace him by "the people".

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Above all, the _____ would not be divided: the Emperor would rule supreme over the subordinate kings, whose obedience to him was mandatory
Louis the Pious.fact: Above all, the Empire would not be divided: the Emperor would rule supreme over the subordinate kings, whose obedience to him was mandatory. With this settlement, Louis attempted to combine his sense for the Empire's unity, supported by the clergy, while at the same time providing positions for all of his sons.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: With this settlement, Louis attempted to combine his sense for the _____'s unity, supported by the clergy, while at the same time providing positions for all of his sons
Louis the Pious.fact: Above all, the Empire would not be divided: the Emperor would rule supreme over the subordinate kings, whose obedience to him was mandatory. With this settlement, Louis attempted to combine his sense for the Empire's unity, supported by the clergy, while at the same time providing positions for all of his sons.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Instead of treating his sons equally in status and land, he elevated his first-born son _____ above his younger brothers and gave him the largest part of the Empire as his share
Louis the Pious.fact: In the event of Lothair dying without sons, one of Louis the Pious's younger sons would be chosen to replace him by "the people". Instead of treating his sons equally in status and land, he elevated his first-born son Lothair above his younger brothers and gave him the largest part of the Empire as his share.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: The decree failed to create order as it omitted _____, who immediately began to conspire
Louis the Pious.fact: The decree failed to create order as it omitted Bernard, who immediately began to conspire.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: When Louis began to issue changes in favor of his second wife Judith's son _____ the Bald, his sons Lothar, Pepin and Louis refused to accept
Louis the Pious.fact: When Louis began to issue changes in favor of his second wife Judith's son Charles the Bald, his sons Lothar, Pepin and Louis refused to accept.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Upon hearing of this, Louis immediately directed his army towards Italy, and headed for _____-sur-Saône
Louis the Pious.fact: Upon hearing of this, Louis immediately directed his army towards Italy, and headed for Chalon-sur-Saône. Intimidated by the emperor's swift action, Bernard met his uncle at Chalon, under invitation, and surrendered.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Intimidated by the emperor's swift action, _____ met his uncle at Chalon, under invitation, and surrendered
Louis the Pious.fact: Intimidated by the emperor's swift action, Bernard met his uncle at Chalon, under invitation, and surrendered. Louis had the sentence commuted to blinding, which was duly carried out; Bernard did not survive the ordeal, however, dying after two days of agony.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Louis had the sentence commuted to blinding, which was duly carried out; _____ did not survive the ordeal, however, dying after two days of agony
Louis the Pious.fact: Intimidated by the emperor's swift action, Bernard met his uncle at Chalon, under invitation, and surrendered. Louis had the sentence commuted to blinding, which was duly carried out; Bernard did not survive the ordeal, however, dying after two days of agony.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He was taken to _____ by Louis, who there had him tried and condemned to death for treason
Louis the Pious.fact: He was taken to Aachen by Louis, who there had him tried and condemned to death for treason.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: In 816, however, the Sorbs rebelled, and were quickly followed by _____, chief of the Obotrites, who was captured and abandoned by his own people, being replaced by Ceadrag in 818
Louis the Pious.fact: In 816, however, the Sorbs rebelled, and were quickly followed by Slavomir, chief of the Obotrites, who was captured and abandoned by his own people, being replaced by Ceadrag in 818.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Soon, _____ too had turned against the Franks and allied with the Danes, who were to become the greatest menace to the Franks in a short time
Louis the Pious.fact: In 816, however, the Sorbs rebelled, and were quickly followed by Slavomir, chief of the Obotrites, who was captured and abandoned by his own people, being replaced by Ceadrag in 818. Soon, Ceadrag too had turned against the Franks and allied with the Danes, who were to become the greatest menace to the Franks in a short time.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: A greater _____ menace was gathering on the southeast
Louis the Pious.fact: A greater Slavic menace was gathering on the southeast.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: There, _____, duke of Slavs in Lower Pannonia, was harassing the border at the Drava and Sava rivers
Louis the Pious.fact: There, Ljudevit, duke of Slavs in Lower Pannonia, was harassing the border at the Drava and Sava rivers.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: The margrave of Friuli, _____, was sent out against him, but he died on campaign and, in 820, his margravate was invaded by Slavs
Louis the Pious.fact: The margrave of Friuli, Cadolah, was sent out against him, but he died on campaign and, in 820, his margravate was invaded by Slavs.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: In 821, an alliance was made with Borna, duke of the _____, and Liudewit was brought to heel
Louis the Pious.fact: In 821, an alliance was made with Borna, duke of the Dalmatia, and Liudewit was brought to heel.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: On the far southern edge of his great realm, Louis had to control the _____ princes of Benevento whom Charlemagne had never subjugated
Louis the Pious.fact: On the far southern edge of his great realm, Louis had to control the Lombard princes of Benevento whom Charlemagne had never subjugated.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He extracted promises from _____ IV and Sico, but to no effect
Louis the Pious.fact: He extracted promises from Princes Grimoald IV and Sico, but to no effect.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: The expedition made its way back north, where it narrowly escaped an ambush attempt arranged by the _____ in the pass of Roncevaux thanks to the precautions he took, i.e
Louis the Pious.fact: The expedition made its way back north, where it narrowly escaped an ambush attempt arranged by the Basques in the pass of Roncevaux thanks to the precautions he took, i.e.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Seguin was replaced by _____, who was dispossessed in 818 by the emperor
Louis the Pious.fact: Seguin was replaced by Lupus III, who was dispossessed in 818 by the emperor.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: In 820 an assembly at _____-sur-Oise decided to send an expedition against the Cordoban caliphate (827)
Louis the Pious.fact: In 820 an assembly at Quierzy-sur-Oise decided to send an expedition against the Cordoban caliphate (827).

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: The counts in charge of the army, Hugh, count of Tours, and _____, count of Orléans, were slow in acting and the expedition came to naught
Louis the Pious.fact: The counts in charge of the army, Hugh, count of Tours, and Matfrid, count of Orléans, were slow in acting and the expedition came to naught.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Ermengarde was the daughter of _____, the duke of Hesbaye
Louis the Pious.fact: Ermengarde was the daughter of Ingerman, the duke of Hesbaye.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: It took many months for his courtiers and advisors to convince him to remarry, but eventually he did, in 820, to Judith, daughter of Welf, count of _____
Louis the Pious.fact: It took many months for his courtiers and advisors to convince him to remarry, but eventually he did, in 820, to Judith, daughter of Welf, count of Altdorf.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: In 823 _____ gave birth to a son, who was named Charles
Louis the Pious.fact: It took many months for his courtiers and advisors to convince him to remarry, but eventually he did, in 820, to Judith, daughter of Welf, count of Altdorf. In 823 Judith gave birth to a son, who was named Charles.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: At Worms in 829, Louis gave _____ to Charles, with the title of king or duke (historians differ on this), thus enraging his son and co-emperor Lothair, whose promised share was thereby diminished
Louis the Pious.fact: At Worms in 829, Louis gave Alemannia to Charles, with the title of king or duke (historians differ on this), thus enraging his son and co-emperor Lothair, whose promised share was thereby diminished.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Ebbo and _____ abandoned the emperor at that point, Bernard having risen to greater heights than either of them
Louis the Pious.fact: Ebbo and Hildwin abandoned the emperor at that point, Bernard having risen to greater heights than either of them.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Agobard, _____ of Lyon, and Jesse, bishop of Amiens, too, opposed the redivision of the empire and lent their episcopal prestige to the rebels
Louis the Pious.fact: Agobard, Archbishop of Lyon, and Jesse, bishop of Amiens, too, opposed the redivision of the empire and lent their episcopal prestige to the rebels.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: In 830, at Wala's insistence that _____ of Septimania was plotting against him, Pepin of Aquitaine led an army of Gascons, with the support of the Neustrian magnates, all the way to Paris
Louis the Pious.fact: With the urging of the vengeful Wala and the cooperation of his brothers, Lothair accused Judith of having committed adultery with Bernard of Septimania, even suggesting Bernard to be the true father of Charles. Ebbo and Hildwin abandoned the emperor at that point, Bernard having risen to greater heights than either of them.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: At Verberie, Louis the _____ joined him
Louis the Pious.fact: At Verberie, Louis the German joined him.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: At that time, the emperor returned from another campaign in _____ to find his empire at war with itself
Louis the Pious.fact: At that time, the emperor returned from another campaign in Brittany to find his empire at war with itself.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: He marched as far as _____ègne, an ancient royal town, before being surrounded by Pepin's forces and captured
Louis the Pious.fact: He marched as far as Compiègne, an ancient royal town, before being surrounded by Pepin's forces and captured.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Judith was incarcerated at _____ and Bernard fled to Barcelona
Louis the Pious.fact: Judith was incarcerated at Poitiers and Bernard fled to Barcelona.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Lothair was pardoned, but disgraced and banished to _____
Louis the Pious.fact: Lothair was pardoned, but disgraced and banished to Italy.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Pepin returned to _____ and Judith—after being forced to humiliate herself with a solemn oath of innocence—to Louis's court
Louis the Pious.fact: Then Lothair finally set out with a large Lombard army, but Louis had promised his sons Louis the German and Pepin of Aquitaine greater shares of the inheritance, prompting them to shift loyalties in favour of their father. Pepin returned to Aquitaine and Judith—after being forced to humiliate herself with a solemn oath of innocence—to Louis's court.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Only Wala was severely dealt with, making his way to a secluded monastery on the shores of _____
Louis the Pious.fact: Only Wala was severely dealt with, making his way to a secluded monastery on the shores of Lake Geneva.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: Although Hilduin, abbot of _____, was exiled to Paderborn and Elisachar and Matfrid were deprived of their honours north of the Alps, they did not lose their freedom
Louis the Pious.fact: Although Hilduin, abbot of Saint Denis, was exiled to Paderborn and Elisachar and Matfrid were deprived of their honours north of the Alps, they did not lose their freedom.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: The disaffected _____ was summoned to his father's court, where he was so poorly received he left against his father's orders
Louis the Pious.fact: Pepin returned to Aquitaine and Judith—after being forced to humiliate herself with a solemn oath of innocence—to Louis's court. The disaffected Pepin was summoned to his father's court, where he was so poorly received he left against his father's orders.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: At Jonac, he declared _____ king of Aquitaine and deprived Pepin (he was less harsh with the younger Louis), restoring the whole rest of the empire to Lothair, not yet involved in the civil war
Louis the Pious.fact: At Jonac, he declared Charles king of Aquitaine and deprived Pepin (he was less harsh with the younger Louis), restoring the whole rest of the empire to Lothair, not yet involved in the civil war. His ministers had been in contact with Pepin and may have convinced him and Louis the German to rebel, promising him Alemannia, the kingdom of Charles.

Louis the Pious.subject: Indian Literature & Poets
Louis the Pious.question: His ministers had been in contact with Pepin and may have convinced him and Louis the German to rebel, promising him _____, the kingdom of Charles
Louis the Pious.fact: His ministers had been in contact with Pepin and may have convinced him and Louis the German to rebel, promising him Alemannia, the kingdom of Charles.
